messages:
sara-ops: Heads up — seeing a provisioning spike in us-east2 after the 570 driver rollout. ~12 nodes stuck at boot after DKMS build step, kernel modules failing to load.

jon-infra: which kernel series? did we pick 6.1 or 5.15 for that pool?

sara-ops: 6.1 (image-builder: linux-6.1.12). Logs from one node: 
```
DKMS: build error for nvidia-570.12: make: *** [modules] Error 2
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.1.12
systemd-udevd[1]: Timed out waiting for device initialization
nvlink: no device found
```

kevin-ml: seeing NCCL WARN on some recovered nodes: `NCCL WARN NET/Socket : failed to connect` — might be missing `nv_peer_mem` or peer memory modules. Also a couple show `nvidia-uvm: failed to map shmem`.

tess-sre: suggestion: cordon the remaining unprovisioned nodes in that pool and rollback the driver to 565 for stability. We can run a small repro canary for 570 in a separate pool.

jon-infra: +1 to cordon. I'll tell the provisioner to stop rolling into us-east2.

jon-infra: `provisioner-bot: stop-roll us-east2 2376543210`

provisioner-bot: ack — stopping current driver rollout in us-east2. 8 nodes remained to be processed.

sara-ops: quick test: rolling back to 565 on one stuck node brought it to boot but 3 still fail during initramfs with `udev settle timeout`.

tess-sre: are those nodes using encrypted root or extra initramfs hooks? seen cases where DKMS builds slow down initramfs and the systemd-udev settle timer expires.

kevin-ml: on a few nodes the dmesg shows `nvidia: kernel module verification failed` and `nvidia: module signature mismatch`. Could be DKMS signing or header mismatch between packaged headers and runtime kernel.

jon-infra: plan: (1) cordon affected nodes (done), (2) stop rollout (done), (3) build repro image with 570 + DKMS debug flags + keep debug shell in initramfs, (4) smoke-test in isolated canary with identical kernel + headers.

sara-ops: I'll create a node list and collect `journalctl -b` logs and `dkms status` for each. Also tagging kernel team for header ABI check.

kevin-ml: note: some pod logs show `failed to allocate nvlink` and `failed to map uvm` — customers running multi-GPU jobs will hit these as scheduling retries. Treat them as degraded GPU health.

jon-infra: if you want to reproduce locally, try: 
```
sudo apt-get install linux-headers-6.1.12
DKMS_BUILD=1 make -C /usr/src/nvidia-570.12 modules
journalctl -b -u systemd-udevd -e
modprobe --first-time nvidia || true
```

tess-sre: quick workaround for schedulers: taint nodes `gpu.provision=soft-failure:NoSchedule` so pods don't land on half-provisioned machines. :thumbsup:

provisioner-bot: helper — marking nodes with tag `rollback-565` and preventing autoscaler from reusing them for 2 hours.

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2023-4542 — GPU provisioning failures in us-east2. Priority: P2.

jon-infra: action owners: jon-infra -> rollback automation + stop-gap deploy, sara-ops -> node list + logs + repro images, kevin-ml -> NCCL/uvm triage and test matrix.

kevin-ml: also expanding smoke tests to include `modprobe nvidia`, `nvidia-smi` and a small NCCL peer test post-provision.

jon-infra: add to postmortem checklist: validate kernel header packaging, DKMS test matrix (drivers 565/570 across kernels 5.15/6.1), provisioner health checks to run `modprobe nvidia` before marking node healthy.

sara-ops: will DM on-call infra with node IDs and keep this thread updated with repro image results. Thanks all. :eyes:
